title: Prayers of every tradition
lede: Mantras, prayers, hymns and chants from many traditions, each with its own words in its own script, a readable pronunciation, its meaning and how it can be used. Arranged by the seven planetary days, and open to everyone.

how.title: How to use this library
paras: The library follows the seven planetary days, a week shared across the world: almost everywhere the days are named for the same seven lights. Monday is the Moon’s day for Selene, Chandra and Tsukuyomi alike; Friday belongs to Venus, Aphrodite, Freyja and Shukra. Each day gathers what suits it, from many traditions. A prayer may be practised on any day, and many are kept on no particular day at all.
You can also come in by tradition, by what you need, or by the kind of text: a mantra, a prayer, a hymn, a chant, a verse or a sutra.
The planetary correspondences are traditional symbolism, not a claim that a planet changes how anyone feels. A person’s circumstances and lived experience are their own.

Every text is given in its own language and script, with a readable pronunciation: a practical guide, not a replacement for learning the sounds from someone who keeps the tradition. In Sanskrit the sacred syllable is written AUM.

Nothing is invented. Each tradition’s own prayer, hymn, chant or invocation is given where one is documented, with its source. Where a figure’s prayers belong to their own community, or are not reliably published, the library honours the figure and says so plainly, rather than make something up.
Repetition counts are optional; one careful recitation can mean more than many said mechanically. Where a text is lineage-held or needs a teacher, the library says so.

rhythm.title: A simple rhythm
rhythm.text: One opening prayer, one main mantra, prayer or verse, and one closing intention. You do not need to recite everything listed for a day: choose what genuinely fits your intention and your tradition, or none.

labels.title: What the labels mean
labels.openText: A devotional prayer or verse anyone may recite.
labels.guidanceText: Seed syllables, tantric or lineage-held: learn its sounds and use from a qualified teacher. The text is shown for study.
labels.variantText: Given as Sarvakali and her teacher keep it. It is not a published text, and it is kept exactly as given, not corrected toward another version.
labels.verifyText: The wording in the source list could not be matched to a published text, so it is held back until Sarvakali confirms it. Its meaning is given.
labels.draftedText: Purpose and use written for this library, to be approved by Sarvakali.
labels.honouredText: A figure honoured in this library whose prayers belong to their own community or are not reliably published. No text is invented; the notes say who they are and how to learn respectfully.

searchHint: A name, a word of the meaning, a tradition or an intention
include: Include texts to learn with guidance
none: Nothing matches. Try fewer words, or another tradition or day.

mantra.supports: What it can support in reflection
mantra.supplied: As supplied in the source list
mantra.noAudio: A recording by Sarvakali will be added here.
mantra.chantLede: Choose how many times. Tap the circle, the button, or press space for each repetition.
mantra.doneChant: Complete. It is in your practice for today.

care: Some of these prayers touch grief, illness and fear. They are spiritual practice, never a replacement for medical or psychological care. If you are struggling, please also reach out to a doctor or counsellor; in India, Tele-MANAS is free on 14416, day and night.
